bifrost: springboard/ui/src/extensions.rs (Scene, Registry, present, browser, to_lines); springboard/sdk/src/share.rs, springboard/src/shell/sharing.rs (manifest-declared share targets); springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (app-declared actions); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (app sandbox)
summary: ExtensionKit lets a third-party app extension supply a custom UI that the host app presents out of process, and lets the user enable or disable extensions. BifrOSt now has a pure model of extension scenes, host presentation and the user's enable and disable choices (springboard/ui/src/extensions.rs), but no out-of-process hosting and no drawn browser UI. The share target list and App Intents remain the only app-facing extension-like pieces.

features.feature: Extension-based UI in a host app (remote views)
features.apple: ExtensionKit: Including extension-based UI in your interface (article)
features.bifrost: none; springboard/sdk/src/view/app.rs is in-process (ControllerHost); springboard/ui/src/extensions.rs Registry::present picks the scene a host would show
features.note: No out-of-process view hosting between apps. Views are built and drawn inside the app that owns them. The model only decides which declared scene is presented.
An app can declare a scene (extension point, identifier, title) and a host can list it. The scene has no content type that a host renders, and no builder syntax.
Scene::new validates the point, identifier and title. There is no connection acceptance (accept(connection:)) and no extension-level configuration object.

features.feature: Host view controller for remote extension views
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/extensions.rs (Presentation, Registry::present); springboard/sdk/src/view/app.rs:40 ControllerHost<C> hosts a view controller in the same process only
features.note: The host decision is modelled: an enabled scene, or the placeholder when none is enabled (placeholderView). Nothing loads or isolates another app's view, and there is no activation or deactivation delegate.

features.apple: EXAppExtensionBrowserViewController; Displaying the app extensions available to your app (article)
features.note: The browser list model groups scenes by extension point and keeps disabled ones. The user's choice persists across uninstalls and restarts. No shell surface draws the list yet.

features.feature: Share targets provided by other apps
features.apple: Share extensions (ExtensionKit host of ExtensionFoundation share UI)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (show_picker); springboard/src/shell/sharing.rs (targets from manifest handles and schemes)
features.note: Other apps can receive shared items when they declare handles or schemes in their manifest. Apps cannot ship their own share UI or a share view that the picker hosts. docs/bifrost-ui.md 'Share sheet' lists share-sheet extensions as a gap.

features.feature: Actions declared by apps for other surfaces
features.apple: App Intents (separate from ExtensionKit; listed for context)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (App::intents, perform_intent over the control socket)
features.note: Apps declare typed actions and entities, but the shell does not host any extension UI for them.

features.feature: Process isolation for third-party app code
features.apple: Extension processes launched and sandboxed by the system (ExtensionFoundation runtime)
features.note: The OS sandboxes apps, but no SDK API lets an app load another app's extension process.

gaps: No out-of-process remote view hosting: ControllerHost in springboard/sdk/src/view/app.rs runs in the owner's process only, and no shell surface loads a scene declared by another app (AppExtensionScene, EXHostViewController).
No drawn enable and disable browser: Registry::browser models the list, but no shell surface shows it (EXAppExtensionBrowserViewController).
No scene content type and no connection acceptance (AppExtensionSceneConfiguration accept(connection:)), so a declared scene carries a title and no UI.
No host activation and deactivation delegate (EXHostViewControllerDelegate).
Share sheet targets are limited to apps with manifest handles or schemes; app-supplied share extensions are missing (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Share sheet).
